cards.text: The LORD is talking to His people through the prophet Malachi. “Your words against Me have been harsh,” says the LORD, and He says they ask, “What have we spoken against You?” Friend, that's like getting called out in the group chat and typing “What did I say?” while the receipts are scrolled up RIGHT THERE.

cards.question: The LORD tells His people exactly what they said against Him. What did they say about serving God?

cards.text: They said they kept His requirements and walked mournfully before the LORD of Hosts, and for what? It's like showing up early to work every single day for a year, and the boss still can't remember your NAME.

cards.question: The people complained that evildoers were getting caught and punished by God.

cards.text: But at that time those who feared the LORD spoke with one another, and the LORD listened and heard them. Friend, nobody heard a WORD I said for years in the back of a junk drawer, so trust me, I know how big that is.

cards.question: So a scroll of ___ was written before the LORD about those who feared Him and honored His name.

cards.text: Then the LORD of Hosts says they will be His, on the day He prepares His treasured possession. Not junk-drawer stuff, friend. TREASURED.

cards.question: On that day, how will the LORD treat the people who fear Him?

answers.text: Spare them like a man spares his son
Pay them like a man pays his workers
Move them to a new land of their own

cards.question: The LORD says His people will again distinguish between the ___ and the wicked, between those who serve God and those who do not.

cards.text: Then the LORD of Hosts says the day is coming, and it's burning like a furnace. I've stood in front of hot ovens my whole life, friend, and not ONE of them comes close to this.

cards.question: On that day, all the arrogant and every evildoer will be ___.

cards.text: The LORD says not a root or branch will be left to them. But then He turns to the ones who fear His name, and the whole picture flips.

cards.question: For those who fear the LORD's name, something will rise with healing in its wings. What is it?
Those who fear the LORD's name will also go out and ___ like calves from the stall.

cards.text: Calves bursting out of the stall, that's me every morning when the ovens warm up, hopping around on my gold base like I just got renewed YESTERDAY. Then the LORD says they will trample the wicked.

cards.question: The LORD says the wicked will be ashes under the soles of the feet of those who fear His name.

cards.text: Now the LORD tells His people to remember something. Not something new, friend. Something they've had a long time.

cards.question: What does the LORD tell His people to remember?

answers.text: The law of His servant Moses
The songs of His servant David
The dreams of His servant Joseph

cards.text: That's the statutes and ordinances He commanded Moses at Horeb for all Israel. Then the LORD looks ahead to the great and awesome Day of the LORD, and says He'll send someone before it comes.

cards.question: Who will the LORD send before the great and awesome Day of the LORD?
Elijah will turn the hearts of the ___ to their children, and the hearts of the ___ to their fathers.

cards.text: Otherwise, the LORD says, He will come and strike the land with a curse. And that's the very last line of the whole book of Malachi, friend.

findings.problem: The joke compares serving God to working for a boss who can't remember your name. That casts God as a forgetful boss and backs up the people's complaint, which the LORD has just called harsh (3:13). It also cuts against the passage's point that the LORD does listen and remember (3:16).

rule.text: His humor never targets God, Jesus, Scripture or the Marriage Supper.

findings.problem: No card tells the baker what 3:15 says: "So now we call the arrogant blessed" and that evildoers prosper. The true/false card only says evildoers weren't punished. Stop 2 card 2 then names "all the arrogant" without this setup, so the contrast between 3:15 and 4:1 is lost.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: "Nobody heard a WORD I said for years in the back of a junk drawer" contradicts his backstory. In the drawer he welcomed and calmed every newcomer, starting with the can opener, and the others held their breath with him. The line changes his drawer years instead of drawing on them.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: Card 1 says the day is "burning like a furnace." That setup rules out "stone" and "iron," since neither burns, so "stubble" is the only answer left. The wrong answers should be things that could also fit a fire and are not near-matches for stubble.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This is a which-thing question. "A dove of peace" is a later symbol, not a detail from the Bible. "A cloud of glory" is also not a phrase the Bible uses. Both wrong answers should be real details from Scripture.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: The opening card says the LORD is speaking "through the prophet Malachi." That fact comes from Malachi 1:1, which is outside the passage. The card cites only Malachi 3:13, so this fact has no reference.
findings.question: The docs allow facts from outside the passage "with their reference," but a story card's verses field must run from the first verse it uses to the last. How should a story card cite an outside-passage fact like Malachi 1:1? Should it go in the verses field, in the card text, or nowhere, given that a range like Malachi 1:1-3:13 would be wrong?
